rules: Every referenced claim must obey permitted_use and limitations.
Access/closure, biological occurrence, quantitative magnitude, and legal regulation are separate evidence dimensions.
Search snippets were discovery aids only; ledger URLs point to the underlying source.

sources.title: Better Fishing Waters
sources.exact_geography: Named St. Joseph Pier, South Haven Pier, and grouped Grand Haven & Holland Piers
sources.fishing_mode: pier; structure allocation unspecified within each named port
sources.claim_supported: Names seven St. Joseph species, nine South Haven species, and nine species for grouped Grand Haven/Holland piers.
sources.permitted_use: Primary species-inventory evidence; exact for the named pier fishery but not a catch-rate or north/south allocation.
sources.limitations: Holland is grouped with Grand Haven; St. Joseph and South Haven do not distinguish the two pierheads.

sources.title: Creel Sportfishing Estimates dashboard — preserved Pier/Dock extract
sources.exact_geography: Target-port Pier/Dock rows for South Haven, Holland, Lexington, and Harrisville; no row resolved for tested St. Joseph aliases
sources.season_represented: survey months vary by port and year
sources.claim_supported: Preserves monthly effort, catch, and harvest estimates used to identify recurring port Pier/Dock leads.
sources.permitted_use: Primary quantitative inventory and Pass 2 queue; preserve estimate types separately.
sources.limitations: Port estimates may pool multiple structures; survey coverage is incomplete by month/year; a zero outside season is not absence; dashboard port label for St. Joseph was not resolved.

sources.title: Creel Clerks & Angler Surveys
sources.exact_geography: Michigan Great Lakes survey program; current clerk areas include South Haven/St. Joseph, Port Austin/Lexington, and Harrisville/Oscoda
sources.claim_supported: Explains angler interviews and current survey coverage assignments.
sources.permitted_use: Method and coverage context only.
sources.limitations: Does not itself provide species magnitude or exact-structure allocation.

sources.title: Roadmap to Fishing Lake Michigan — accessible version
sources.exact_geography: Lake Michigan ports including Holland/Port Sheldon, Saugatuck/South Haven, and St. Joseph
sources.season_represented: January through October in four seasonal columns
sources.claim_supported: Identifies port-season leads, including cold-season salmonids and warm-season drum.
sources.permitted_use: Seasonal lead generation and conflict checking, never exact-pier magnitude.
sources.limitations: Combines Holland with Port Sheldon and South Haven with Saugatuck; mode is not separated; November-December coverage is not systematic.

sources.title: Roadmap to Fishing Lake Huron — accessible version
sources.exact_geography: Named Harrisville and Lexington ports
sources.season_represented: January through October in four seasonal columns
sources.claim_supported: Lists Harrisville lake trout, steelhead, walleye and fall Atlantic salmon; lists Lexington Atlantic, Chinook, coho, pink, steelhead, lake trout, walleye, and yellow perch by season.
sources.permitted_use: Primary seasonal lead generation, not score magnitude.
sources.limitations: Port-level and mode-mixed; blank cells are not proof of absence; November-December are not systematically represented.

sources.title: 2026 Michigan Fishing Regulations
sources.exact_geography: Michigan Great Lakes, including Lake Michigan MM 6-8 and Lake Huron MH 3-6
sources.claim_supported: Current statewide and Great Lakes rules; Lexington and Harrisville are in MH 3-6 and Holland in MM 6-8.
sources.permitted_use: Legal context and later closure modeling only; no biological magnitude.
sources.limitations: Anglers must check updates and fisheries orders; local posted access restrictions are separate.

sources.title: State parks general rules
sources.exact_geography: Michigan state parks, including Holland State Park
sources.claim_supported: Day-use areas are generally open 8 a.m.-10 p.m.; vehicle entry may require a Recreation Passport.
sources.permitted_use: Primary hours/pass baseline where a park page does not publish a narrower rule.
sources.limitations: Posted closures and site-specific rules control; not a live gate status.

sources.title: Harbors — general rules
sources.exact_geography: Michigan state-managed harbors, including Lexington
sources.claim_supported: Fishing is not allowed in a state harbor unless otherwise posted.
sources.permitted_use: Primary default access rule.
sources.limitations: Local posted permission is required; the page does not map each permitted surface.

sources.publisher: United States Coast Guard Navigation Center
sources.title: Light List Volume VII, Great Lakes
sources.exact_geography: Named aids at St. Joseph, South Haven, Holland, Lexington, and Harrisville
sources.claim_supported: Provides authoritative structure names and coordinates for pierhead and breakwater lights.
sources.permitted_use: Coordinate and structure-identity source only.
sources.limitations: Aid coordinates identify the light, not the legal pedestrian route or fishing permission.

sources.title: Fishing Access
sources.exact_geography: St. Joseph South Pier from Silver Beach
sources.claim_supported: Confirms public South Pier route, USACE ownership/maintenance context, at-own-risk access, and a local species list.
sources.permitted_use: Primary exact-route, safety, and exact-site inventory evidence.
sources.limitations: Generic catfish and whitefish labels are not species-level proof for channel catfish or round whitefish; no catch-rate denominator.

sources.title: Silver Beach County Park
sources.exact_geography: 101 Broad Street and South Pier; also identifies North Pier route from Tiscornia
sources.claim_supported: Dawn-to-dusk park hours, May-September parking fees, no overnight parking, free walk-in, and separate routes to both piers.
sources.permitted_use: Primary access, fees, hours, and boundary source.
sources.limitations: Park hours govern the approach; the USACE pier is outside county park property and conditions can make access unsafe.

sources.publisher: City of St. Joseph Parks and Recreation
sources.title: Tiscornia Beach facility details
sources.publication_date: current page; status open on review date
sources.exact_geography: 80 Ridgeway Street; St. Joseph North Pier
sources.claim_supported: Identifies the North Pier/lighthouse walkway and fishing use; status displayed Open.
sources.permitted_use: Primary exact-route and published-status evidence.
sources.limitations: Reservation-grid hours are not established park operating hours; live weather/ice closures still require verification.

sources.publisher: South Haven Area Emergency Services Authority
sources.title: South Haven Beach Safety
sources.exact_geography: South Haven North and South beaches and pierheads
sources.season_represented: May 15-September 15 flag program plus year-round closure authority
sources.claim_supported: Both beaches access the pierheads; the city may close both piers during red-flag/high-wave conditions and violators are subject to arrest.
sources.permitted_use: Primary safety closure and access-control evidence.
sources.limitations: The page is not a real-time physical inspection and does not publish complete beach hours or parking rates.

sources.publisher: South Haven/Van Buren County Convention & Visitors Bureau
sources.title: Where to Fish in South Haven: 5 Easy-Access Spots for Shore Anglers
sources.exact_geography: North/South Piers, Harborwalk, Black River Park, and SHOUT Park
sources.claim_supported: Separates both piers, lower Harborwalk seawalls, and two upstream Black River fishing platforms; names broad pier species.
sources.permitted_use: Secondary structure inventory and current fishing-use corroboration.
sources.limitations: Promotional and qualitative; generic bass/catfish/trout labels and no standardized effort.

sources.title: Harborwalk — City of South Haven
sources.exact_geography: South Haven Harborwalk from North Beach to South Beach
sources.claim_supported: Provides the pier-to-pier route and GPS point 42°24.18900, -86°16.57080.
sources.permitted_use: Route identity and coordinate context.
sources.limitations: Does not designate every seawall segment for fishing or provide closure status.

sources.title: Black River Park Marina — City of South Haven
sources.exact_geography: Dunkley Avenue, Black River Park
sources.season_represented: all four seasons shown; facilities may be seasonal
sources.claim_supported: City-owned marina access, parking terms, and GPS 42°24.53280, -86°16.31400.
sources.permitted_use: Boundary review for a separately excluded upstream platform.
sources.limitations: This is about one mile upstream and cannot establish pier opportunity.

sources.title: Holland State Park
sources.exact_geography: 2459 Ottawa Beach Road; north side of Holland channel
sources.fishing_mode: state-park channel walkway and north pier
sources.claim_supported: Fishing is popular along the Lake Michigan channel walkway; vehicle entry requires a Recreation Passport.
sources.permitted_use: Primary north-route boundary and access evidence.
sources.limitations: Does not authorize the south route or provide species-specific catch magnitude.

sources.title: Boat Launches + Fishing Piers
sources.exact_geography: Holland State Park breakwall and pier
sources.claim_supported: Confirms fishing use from the breakwall and pier at Holland State Park.
sources.permitted_use: Secondary current-use corroboration.
sources.limitations: No standardized biological data or south-route authorization.

sources.title: Big Red Lighthouse
sources.exact_geography: Holland Harbor south-side pedestrian approaches
sources.claim_supported: States there is currently no walkway access and private property surrounds pedestrian access points.
sources.permitted_use: Current operator evidence to exclude the south route.
sources.limitations: Applies to pedestrian access; does not erase biological observations assigned to the port.

sources.publisher: Michigan Economic Development Corporation / Michigan DNR listing
sources.title: Lexington State Harbor
sources.exact_geography: 7411 Huron Bay Boulevard; Lexington State Harbor
sources.claim_supported: Provides address, 43°15'50 N 82°31'00 W, 108 slips, amenities, and normal season.
sources.permitted_use: Facility identity, address, coordinate, and normal-season context.
sources.limitations: Normal season is superseded by project closures and does not itself identify legal fishing surfaces.

sources.title: Planned upgrades and closures at Lexington State Harbor
sources.exact_geography: Lexington State Harbor marina, breakwall, and boating access site
sources.claim_supported: Entire marina is closed 2026-09-08 through 2027-05-28 for in-water replacement; breakwall repairs occurred in summer 2026; 2027 work may cause intermittent closures.
sources.permitted_use: Primary live release gate and construction evidence.
sources.limitations: The notice does not explicitly map pedestrian breakwater access after 2026-09-08; safe public access must be confirmed directly.

sources.title: Beach Access & Marina
sources.exact_geography: Lexington harbor, Tierney Park, and state-harbor facilities
sources.claim_supported: Provides normal harbormaster hours, launch route, and beach access east of the light.
sources.permitted_use: Primary municipal route context.
sources.limitations: Normal operations are superseded by DNR construction closures; page does not designate fishing surfaces.

sources.title: Atlantic salmon
sources.exact_geography: Lexington Harbor and other Michigan program waters
sources.claim_supported: Identifies Lexington Harbor as an experimental Atlantic salmon fishery stocked each spring.
sources.permitted_use: Primary management lead; corroborates but does not alone quantify pier catch.
sources.limitations: Stocking does not by itself establish catch magnitude or safe current access.

sources.publisher: Great Lakes Fishery Commission Fish Stocking Information System; event reported by Michigan DNR
sources.title: Stocking Event 202565056
sources.exact_geography: Lexington Harbor at reported coordinate 43.2675, -82.5266
sources.claim_supported: Records 26,667 age-1 landlocked Atlantic salmon stocked at Lexington Harbor.
sources.permitted_use: Primary stocking context and coordinate corroboration.
sources.limitations: Stocking is not exact-pier catch evidence and cannot set opportunity magnitude.

sources.publisher: Michigan Department of Natural Resources Law Enforcement Division
sources.title: Conservation officer biweekly report 11/24/2024-12/7/2024
sources.exact_geography: Lexington Harbor
sources.claim_supported: Documents Atlantic salmon physically present and being caught at Lexington Harbor, although by illegal snagging.
sources.permitted_use: Exact-harbor occurrence and timing only.
sources.limitations: Illegal method cannot establish lawful intentional angling quality or catch rate.

sources.publisher: Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Lake Huron Citizens Fishery Advisory Committee
sources.title: Minutes — October 7, 2025
sources.exact_geography: Harrisville Harbor and surrounding port area
sources.fishing_mode: unoccupied marina docks plus mixed port/boat reports
sources.claim_supported: States fishing on unoccupied docks is permitted and reports Chinook/coho caught from them; separately reports area coho, steelhead, lake trout, Chinook, and walleye and discusses possible Atlantic/coho stocking.
sources.permitted_use: Primary advisory record for exact dock permission/catch leads and broader port leads, with modes kept separate.
sources.limitations: Statements are meeting testimony, not a controlled survey; lake trout and walleye statements are not allocated to docks; proposed Atlantic stocking is not an implemented event.

sources.publisher: Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Lake Huron Citizens Fishery Advisory Committee
sources.title: Minutes — October 4, 2022
sources.exact_geography: Harrisville Harbor
sources.fishing_mode: harbor angling; exact surface not allocated
sources.claim_supported: Reports regular fall Chinook, occasional Atlantic salmon, and a winter fishery in Harrisville Harbor.
sources.permitted_use: Exact-harbor occurrence lead for Atlantic salmon and cold-season fishing.
sources.limitations: Advisory testimony does not identify the fishing surface or establish annual recurrence, effort, or legal access.

sources.publisher: Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Lake Huron Citizens Fishery Advisory Committee
sources.title: Minutes — February 1, 2022
sources.exact_geography: Harrisville Harbor
sources.claim_supported: Reports coho caught through the ice in Harrisville Harbor despite no local stocking at that time.
sources.permitted_use: Exact-harbor cold-season lead.
sources.limitations: Advisory testimony; ice safety, access, effort, and recurrence require independent review.

sources.publisher: Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Lake Huron Citizens Fishery Advisory Committee
sources.title: Minutes — January 31, 2023
sources.exact_geography: Harrisville Harbor
sources.claim_supported: Reports six or seven brown trout caught before harbor freeze, including a fish around 28 inches.
sources.permitted_use: Exact-harbor brown-trout recurrence lead.
sources.limitations: Advisory testimony with no effort denominator or precise fishing surface.

sources.title: 2024-2028 Recreation Plan
sources.exact_geography: Harrisville Municipal Marina and harbor
sources.claim_supported: States a fishing program was developed to permit safe harbor fishing while protecting docks and avoiding boaters.
sources.permitted_use: Primary municipal policy context.
sources.limitations: Does not map the designated fishing areas or establish year-round dock access.

sources.title: Harbor Rules and Regulations — 2023
sources.exact_geography: Harrisville Harbor premises
sources.fishing_mode: marina docks and designated fishing areas
sources.claim_supported: Fishing is prohibited within harbor premises except designated areas; permittees may fish from their assigned vessels.
sources.permitted_use: Operator rule controlling dock access.
sources.limitations: Does not publish a current map of designated areas; must be reconciled with 2025 permission for unoccupied docks.

sources.title: Michigan State Harbors Guide — Harrisville Municipal Marina
sources.exact_geography: Harrisville Municipal Marina
sources.claim_supported: Provides facility coordinate 44°39'43 N, 83°16'50 W, normal operating season, and amenities.
sources.permitted_use: Facility coordinate and normal season only.
sources.limitations: Marina season does not establish year-round public dock fishing.

sources.publisher: Great Lakes Fishery Commission Fish Stocking Information System; event reported by Michigan DNR
sources.title: CWT 64-14-84 — Harrisville Harbor stocking event 202666111
sources.exact_geography: Lake Huron, Harrisville Harbor
sources.claim_supported: Records 11,250 age-1 Michigan winter-strain rainbow trout/steelhead stocked at Harrisville Harbor.
sources.permitted_use: Primary stocking lead only.
sources.limitations: Stocking does not establish exact-dock catch magnitude or access.

sources.title: Coded wire tags
sources.exact_geography: Harrisville Harbor, Lexington Harbor, and other Michigan drop-off sites
sources.claim_supported: Confirms fish-head drop-off infrastructure at Harrisville Harbor and Lexington Harbor.
sources.permitted_use: Monitoring infrastructure context only.
sources.limitations: A drop-off site is not evidence that any particular species is caught at that structure.
